name: React.js Production Engineering Track
description: Master modern React 18+ component architecture, JSX syntax, state management, useEffect lifecycle side-effects, custom hooks, Context API, and production web application building.
whatYouLearn: Understand React virtual DOM and component rendering trees
Pass data via immutable Props and manage local State with useState
Synchronize side effects and API data fetching with useEffect
Encapsulate stateful logic using custom React Hooks
Eliminate prop drilling with Context API and state dispatchers
Build a production Shopping Cart and Movie Search Web App
prerequisites: JavaScript ES6+ Full Stack Engine Track

exercises.title: JSX Syntax & Component Rendering
exercises.description: Write functional React components returning valid JSX markup.
exercises.theory: JSX is a syntax extension for JavaScript that looks like HTML. In JSX, class becomes className and all tags must close explicitly.
exercises.objective: Build a functional React header component returning JSX.
requirements: Use className instead of class
Embed variable expressions using single curly braces {}
Export default functional component
hints: JSX single root element or Fragment (<>...</>) wrapper is required

exercises.title: Props & Component Reusability
exercises.description: Pass data down to child components using destructured props.
exercises.theory: Props (properties) pass immutable data down from parent to child components.
exercises.objective: Build a reusable ProductCard component driven by props.
requirements: Destructure props in parameter signature
Set default value for inStock = true
Render conditional badge class based on inStock boolean
hints: Destructuring parameter ({ name, price }) avoids writing props.name repeatedly

exercises.title: State Management with useState
exercises.description: Declare state variables and trigger re-renders using the useState hook.
exercises.theory: useState declares state variables. Calling setter functions triggers component re-rendering with updated state.
exercises.objective: Build an interactive Counter component with increment and decrement handlers.
requirements: Use useState hook initialized with initialValue
Use functional state updater (prev => prev + 1)
Bind click handlers to buttons
hints: Always use functional state updates when next state depends on previous state

exercises.title: Conditional Rendering Patterns
exercises.description: Render UI elements conditionally using ternary operators, logical AND (&&), and early returns.
exercises.theory: Use inline ternary (condition ? A : B) or short-circuit logical AND (condition && <Component />) for conditional UI rendering.
exercises.objective: Render UserDashboard vs LoginPrompt based on isLoggedIn boolean prop.
requirements: Use early return guard clause for !isLoggedIn
Use logical && for user.isAdmin badge
hints: Early returns keep JSX template rendering clean

exercises.title: Rendering Lists with Keys
exercises.description: Render arrays of objects using map() and assign unique keys to list elements.
exercises.theory: When rendering lists in React, each item must have a unique key prop to help the Virtual DOM reconcile list updates efficiently.
exercises.objective: Render a list of course items with unique keys.
exercises.initialCode:
const courses = [{ id: '1', title: 'React' }, { id: '2', title: 'Python' }];
// Render list with keys
requirements: Use array.map() to project list items into JSX
Assign unique key prop matching course.id
hints: Avoid using array index as key when list order can change dynamically

exercises.title: Handling User Input & Controlled Components
exercises.description: Build controlled form inputs bound to React state.
exercises.theory: In controlled components, form input values are driven by React state and updated via onChange handlers.
exercises.objective: Build a controlled login form with email and password state.
requirements: Manage form input object state with useState
Use compute property name handler [e.target.name]: e.target.value
Call e.preventDefault() in submit handler
hints: e.preventDefault() prevents default full-page browser submit refresh

exercises.title: Side Effects & Data Fetching with useEffect
exercises.description: Fetch API data on component mount and handle cleanup using the useEffect hook.
exercises.theory: useEffect synchronizes components with external systems. Dependency array controls when side effect callback re-runs.
exercises.objective: Fetch courses data on component mount using useEffect.
requirements: Use useEffect with empty dependency array []
Handle loading spinner state
Set fetched data in state
hints: Empty array [] ensures side effect runs only once when component mounts

exercises.title: useEffect Dependency Arrays & Cleanup
exercises.description: Manage dependency array triggers and return cleanup functions to prevent memory leaks.
exercises.theory: Returning a function from useEffect defines a cleanup handler executed when the component unmounts or before re-running the effect.
exercises.objective: Build a window resize window listener component with cleanup.
requirements: Attach window resize event listener in useEffect
Return cleanup function removing event listener
hints: Always clean up event listeners, timers, and subscriptions in useEffect returns
exercises.codeExample: useEffect(() => { const timer = setInterval(fn, 1000); return () => clearInterval(timer); }, []);

exercises.title: Custom React Hooks
exercises.description: Extract reusable stateful logic into custom React hooks (useFetch, useLocalStorage).
exercises.theory: Custom hooks are JavaScript functions whose names start with 'use' and can invoke other React hooks to encapsulate reusable state logic.
exercises.objective: Build a custom useLocalStorage hook.
exercises.initialCode: // Create custom useLocalStorage hook
requirements: Name hook function starting with 'use' (useLocalStorage)
Use lazy state initialization with useState(() => ...)
Return tuple array [storedValue, setStoredValue]
hints: Lazy initial state prevents reading from localStorage on every render
exercises.codeExample: const useToggle = (init = false) => { const [v, setV] = useState(init); return [v, () => setV(!v)]; };

exercises.title: Context API & Global State Management
exercises.description: Eliminate prop drilling by creating ThemeContext with createContext and useContext.
exercises.theory: Context API provides a way to share data globally across the component tree without passing props manually down every level.
exercises.objective: Create ThemeContext Provider and consume theme state in child components.
exercises.initialCode:
import { createContext } from 'react';
// Create and consume ThemeContext
requirements: Create context with createContext()
Build ThemeProvider wrapper passing value object
Export custom useTheme hook wrapping useContext(ThemeContext)
hints: Wrap root application inside <ThemeProvider> to make context accessible
exercises.codeExample: const Context = createContext(); const val = useContext(Context);

exercises.title: Reducer Pattern with useReducer
exercises.description: Manage complex state transitions using the useReducer hook.
exercises.theory: useReducer is preferred over useState when managing complex state objects with multiple sub-values and explicit action dispatchers.
exercises.objective: Build a Todo list state reducer handling ADD, TOGGLE, and DELETE actions.
exercises.initialCode:
import { useReducer } from 'react';
// Implement todo reducer
requirements: Write pure reducer function handling switch(action.type)
Use useReducer(todoReducer, initialArray)
Dispatch actions with type and payload
hints: Reducers must remain pure functions without side effects

exercises.title: Performance Optimization: useMemo & useCallback
exercises.description: Memoize expensive calculations with useMemo and callback references with useCallback.
exercises.theory: useMemo caches calculation results, while useCallback caches function references to prevent unnecessary child re-renders.
exercises.objective: Optimize expensive data filtering using useMemo.
exercises.initialCode:
import { useMemo } from 'react';
// Optimize calculation
requirements: Wrap expensive array filter in useMemo
Set dependency array [items, searchQuery]
hints: useMemo re-executes calculation function only when specified dependencies change
exercises.codeExample: const memoized = useMemo(() => compute(a, b), [a, b]);

exercises.title: DOM References with useRef
exercises.description: Access underlying DOM elements directly and store mutable values without triggering re-renders.
exercises.theory: useRef returns a mutable ref object whose .current property persists across re-renders without causing component re-rendering.
exercises.objective: Auto-focus an input element on component mount using useRef.
requirements: Declare ref object with useRef(null)
Attach ref attribute to input element
Call inputRef.current.focus() inside useEffect on mount
hints: inputRef.current points directly to the underlying HTMLInputElement node

exercises.title: React Portals & Modal Dialogs
exercises.description: Render modal dialog overlays outside parent DOM containers using ReactDOM.createPortal.
exercises.theory: React Portals (createPortal) render children into a DOM node existing outside the parent component's DOM hierarchy.
exercises.objective: Build a Modal overlay rendering into document.body.
exercises.initialCode:
import ReactDOM from 'react-dom';
// Build Modal portal
requirements: Use ReactDOM.createPortal(jsx, document.body)
Call e.stopPropagation() on modal card to prevent backdrop click closing
hints: stopPropagation prevents click events inside modal card from closing the overlay

exercises.title: Error Boundaries
exercises.description: Catch JavaScript errors anywhere in child component trees using error boundary class components.
exercises.theory: Error Boundaries are React class components that catch errors in child component trees during rendering and display fallback UI.
exercises.objective: Implement an ErrorBoundary class component.
exercises.initialCode:
import React, { Component } from 'react';
// Create ErrorBoundary
requirements: Define static getDerivedStateFromError method
Implement componentDidCatch for error logging
Render fallback UI when hasError is true
hints: Error boundaries catch rendering errors in child components, not event handler errors

exercises.title: React.memo & Pure Component Optimization
exercises.description: Prevent unnecessary child component re-renders using React.memo.
exercises.theory: React.memo wraps functional components to shallowly compare props, skipping re-renders if props have not changed.
exercises.objective: Wrap a child ListItem component with React.memo.
exercises.initialCode:
import React from 'react';
// Optimize ListItem with React.memo
requirements: Wrap functional component in React.memo()
Log component rendering to demonstrate memoization
hints: Combine React.memo with useCallback on function props for complete optimization

exercises.title: Client-Side Routing Concepts
exercises.description: Simulate client-side view routing based on location hash or state.
exercises.theory: Client-side routing swaps rendered view components based on URL path updates without reloading the HTML page.
exercises.objective: Build a lightweight Router view switcher.
requirements: Write view components Home, Courses, NotFound
Switch rendered component based on path prop
hints: Routing components swap rendered children while sharing global navigation headers

exercises.title: Compound Component Pattern
exercises.description: Design flexible UI component libraries using the Compound Component pattern.
exercises.theory: Compound components share implicit state between parent and child components (e.g. Select and Select.Option).
exercises.objective: Build a Accordion and Accordion.Item compound component.
exercises.initialCode: // Build compound accordion component
requirements: Create shared AccordionContext
Attach Item sub-component directly to main Accordion component object
hints: Attaching sub-components to parent object (Accordion.Item = ...) improves component API ergonomics

exercises.title: Optimistic UI Updates
exercises.description: Implement optimistic UI updates that update local state immediately before API server confirmation.
exercises.theory: Optimistic UI renders changes instantly to enhance perceived performance, rolling back state if the network request fails.
exercises.objective: Build an optimistic Like button with rollback on failure.
requirements: Update state optimistically before API promise resolves
Rollback state to initial values inside catch block on failure
hints: Store previous state values before mutating state so rollback can restore them exactly
exercises.codeExample: setVal(v => v + 1); try { await api(); } catch { setVal(prev); }

exercises.title: Capstone Project: Interactive Shopping Cart App
exercises.description: Build a production-grade Shopping Cart application featuring Context API, useReducer, item additions, quantity updates, total cost calculations, and localStorage persistence.
exercises.theory: This capstone project combines modern React 18+ architecture: useReducer state management, Context API global distribution, custom hooks, and local storage persistence.
exercises.objective: Construct a full Shopping Cart application system.
exercises.initialCode: // Construct Shopping Cart system
requirements: Implement cartReducer with ADD_ITEM, REMOVE_ITEM, and CLEAR_CART actions
Calculate total cost dynamically
Persist cart state in localStorage
hints: Lazy initialization in useReducer (3rd parameter) initializes state from localStorage safely
exercises.codeExample: const total = cart.reduce((a, b) => a + (b.price * b.qty), 0);
